title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 3rd Proof The Uniqueness Of Conveying The Message Summoning And Faith

questions.question: What strong qualities did the passage say he showed when he delivered the message and called people to the truth?
questions.answer: He showed steady commitment, firmness, and bravery.

questions.question: Who stood against him, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Powerful governments, other religions, and even his own people, clan, and uncle opposed him.

questions.question: How did he respond to that opposition?
questions.answer: He did not show fear, panic, or wavering.

questions.question: What result is given as proof of his success in calling people to Islam?
questions.answer: He challenged the world and Islam became dominant in a major way.

questions.question: What does that success show about him?
questions.answer: It shows that no one can equal him in delivering the message and inviting people to the truth.

questions.question: How is his faith described in the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as extremely strong, wide-reaching, and full of certainty and conviction.

questions.question: What kinds of ideas could not shake his faith?
questions.answer: The popular beliefs of his time, philosophers’ ideas, and religious teachings that opposed him could not weaken it.

questions.question: What effect did hostility and denial have on his inner confidence?
questions.answer: They did not create doubt, hesitation, weakness, or anxiety in him.

questions.question: Which group is mentioned first as drawing from his belief and reaching high levels of faith?
questions.answer: The Companions are mentioned first.

questions.question: What does the passage say later saintly people of all ages did with his example of faith?
questions.answer: They benefited from it and saw him as the highest example of belief.

questions.question: What conclusion did the traveler reach about lying and hypocrisy?
questions.answer: He concluded that such faults could not belong to someone with that law, worship, prayer, call to truth, and faith.

questions.question: Name two areas besides faith that are listed at the end as signs of his truthfulness.
questions.answer: His sacred law and his devotion in worship.

questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: It explains why his truthfulness is proven by his courage, his success in preaching, and the unmatched strength of his faith.

questions.question: In what work of his mission did he remain firm?
questions.answer: He remained firm in delivering the message and inviting people to the truth.

questions.question: What makes his courage stand out even more?
questions.answer: He faced enemies from many directions, including people close to him.

questions.question: Why is the mention of his own tribe and uncle important?
questions.answer: It shows the pressure was personal as well as public.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that he showed no hesitation?
questions.answer: We can infer that he was completely sure of his mission.

questions.question: How does the passage connect his public success with his special rank?
questions.answer: It presents his worldwide success as evidence that he has no equal in this mission.

questions.question: What words in the passage point to the depth of his iman?
questions.answer: It says his faith had great strength, certainty, breadth, and high conviction.

questions.question: What failed to put even a small crack in his faith?
questions.answer: Opposing beliefs, philosophical ideas, and hostile rejection all failed.

questions.question: According to the passage, who recognized him as the highest model of faith?
questions.answer: The saintly people across the ages, especially beginning with the Companions, recognized him that way.

questions.question: What does “drawn on his fountain of belief” mean in simple words?
questions.answer: It means they took guidance and spiritual strength from his faith.

questions.question: What final judgment did the traveler’s mind confirm about his character?
questions.answer: It confirmed that deceit and lying could not be part of him.

questions.question: Why does the passage gather many qualities together in the last sentence?
questions.answer: It uses all of them together to build a strong case for his honesty and truthfulness.

questions.question: What duty was he carrying out in this passage?
questions.answer: He was delivering Allah’s message and calling people to the truth.

questions.question: Which three character traits are highlighted first?
questions.answer: Steadiness, firmness, and courage.

questions.question: What kind of enemies did he face?
questions.answer: He faced hostile opposition from major powers, other religions, and people from his own background.

questions.question: What emotional weakness does the passage say he did not show at all?
questions.answer: He did not show fear or nervous uncertainty.

questions.question: How does the passage use outcomes to support its point?
questions.answer: It points to his success in confronting the world and spreading Islam as evidence.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the relationship between certainty and action?
questions.answer: It shows that deep certainty gives a person strength to keep going without wavering.

questions.question: How is his faith shown to be different from ordinary faith?
questions.answer: It is presented as broader, stronger, and more certain than anyone else’s.

questions.question: What sources of opposition tried to challenge his belief?
questions.answer: The common views of the time, scholars of philosophy, and religious authorities tried to oppose it.

questions.question: Did these attacks damage his trust and confidence? Explain.
questions.answer: No. The passage says they could not create even the smallest doubt or weakness.

questions.question: What role do the Companions play in this argument?
questions.answer: They are presented as leading examples of believers who drew from his faith.

questions.question: What does the passage say saintly people from later times believed about his iman?
questions.answer: They believed his level of faith was the highest.

questions.question: Based on the whole passage, why does the traveler reject the idea that he could lie?
questions.answer: Because someone with unmatched law, worship, prayer, calling, and faith would not be a person of falsehood or double-dealing.

questions.question: According to the passage, what was special about the way he called people to the truth?
questions.answer: He did it with unmatched strength and bravery.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the amount of opposition he faced?
questions.answer: It says the opposition was very wide and very hostile.

questions.question: Which close family relation is specifically named among those who opposed him?
questions.answer: His uncle is specifically named.

questions.question: What does his lack of fear suggest about his heart?
questions.answer: It suggests his heart was firm and fully convinced.

questions.question: What historical result is used as evidence in the passage?
questions.answer: The passage points to his successful challenge to the world and the rise of Islam.

questions.question: How is his faith described in terms of size and reach?
questions.answer: It is described as broad and world-illuminating.

questions.question: What kinds of thinkers are mentioned as unable to shake him?
questions.answer: Philosophers and religious leaders are mentioned.

questions.question: What four inner problems could not enter his faith?
questions.answer: Doubt, hesitation, weakness, and anxiety could not enter it.

questions.question: Who are said to be foremost in levels of belief?
questions.answer: The Companions are said to be foremost.

questions.question: What did saintly believers of every age do in relation to his faith?
questions.answer: They took from it and accepted him as the greatest example of faith.

questions.question: What overall point does this make about his faith?
questions.answer: It makes the point that his faith has no equal.

questions.question: How does the traveler use all these proofs at the end?
questions.answer: He uses them to confirm that falsehood and insincerity do not fit such a person.

questions.question: What two major themes about him are emphasized in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage emphasizes his fearless delivery of the message and the unmatched power of his faith.

questions.question: What did he keep doing even when many groups fought against him?
questions.answer: He kept calling people to the truth without backing down.

questions.question: What does the passage show by saying he had no sign of panic or fear?
questions.answer: It shows he was completely brave and steady.

questions.question: What larger achievement is mentioned after describing his courage?
questions.answer: His success in confronting the world and establishing Islam strongly is mentioned.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the certainty of his faith?
questions.answer: It portrays it as amazing, firm, and beyond normal human levels.

questions.question: What could not disturb his certainty, even with strong opposition?
questions.answer: The dominant beliefs of the age and the teachings of opposing thinkers could not disturb it.

questions.question: Which believers are placed at the front of the saintly people in this passage?
questions.answer: The Companions are placed first among them.

questions.question: What was their view of his level of belief?
questions.answer: They saw it as the highest level.

questions.question: What list of qualities supports the traveler’s final conclusion?
questions.answer: His unique law, unmatched Islam, excellent worship, remarkable prayer, universal call to truth, and miraculous faith support it.

questions.question: State the traveler’s final conclusion in simple words.
questions.answer: He concluded that a person with all those qualities cannot be a liar or a hypocrite.

questions.question: In the passage, what was he inviting people toward?
questions.answer: He was inviting people toward the truth.

questions.question: What personal strengths helped him do that?
questions.answer: Strong resolve, firmness, and courage helped him.

questions.question: How serious was the resistance against him?
questions.answer: It was severe and came from major outside groups and from his own relatives and community.

questions.question: What detail shows that the pressure did not break him emotionally?
questions.answer: He showed no sign of fear, worry, or wavering.

questions.question: What proof from history is given for his unmatched mission?
questions.answer: His success against worldwide opposition and the triumph of Islam is given as proof.

questions.question: How many parts of his faith are praised in one sentence of the passage?
questions.answer: Four parts are praised: its strength, certainty, breadth, and high conviction.

questions.question: What groups of ideas were unable to weaken his belief?
questions.answer: The leading beliefs of the world, philosophical teachings, and religious teachings were unable to weaken it.

questions.question: What is the meaning of saying his faith lit up the world?
questions.answer: It means his belief had a powerful, far-reaching influence on people everywhere.

questions.question: Who followed him and reached high ranks in belief?
questions.answer: The Companions and saintly believers through the ages followed him and reached high ranks.

questions.question: What does their agreement add to the argument?
questions.answer: Their agreement strengthens the claim that his faith was the highest and truest.

questions.question: Which acts and qualities are gathered together before the final judgment?
questions.answer: His law, Islam, worship, supplication, call to truth, and faith are gathered together.

questions.question: What final moral conclusion is made about his character?
questions.answer: A person with those qualities has no room for lies or two-faced behavior.
